transcript: Today I saw The Doctor at Park Avenue Armory. In this play, the titular character, a doctor, makes a decision in the final moments of a patient's life that raises ethical questions, one of which is framed as a medicine versus religion debate. This is only the beginning of an almost 3 hour play that explores plenty of tough questions related to ethics and identity. The subject matter is very intense, and nobody's Painted is particularly morally good or bad. I thought this play was great. It was complex and constructed in ways that continue to push the audience to consider and reconsider throughout. I would definitely recommend going with a friend to this one because there will be so much to discuss afterwards. With that, another program for my collection.
